voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.title: Welcome to the Guggenheim Bilbao
tracks.where: On the Museum plaza with Puppy, the giant terrier of flowers, in view, standing aside from the broad stairway so people can pass [O1, O20, O21].
tracks.what: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa), architect Frank O. Gehry (Toronto 1929 – Santa Monica 2025); opened October 1997 (royal inauguration 18 Oct, public 19 Oct); one of the Guggenheim museums with New York and Venice, run by Basque institutions with the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation. Guide scope: the building and the works on long-term view (Koons, Serra, Holzer, Chillida, Bourgeois, Kapoor, Nakaya, Klein, Buren), all credited Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: Where you are, who built it and why, what this guide covers, the route in three lengths, and the only two timings you need.

tracks.title: Museum plaza — Puppy, the guard dog in bloom
tracks.where: On the Museum plaza, facing Puppy, the twelve-metre West Highland terrier covered in flowering plants; stand where you can see all of him, clear of the broad stairway [O1, O2, O25].
tracks.what: Jeff Koons, Puppy, 1992, stainless steel, soil and flowering plants, 1240 × 1240 × 820 cm, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa (artist's proof; edition 1 at the Brant Foundation, Greenwich, Connecticut). Earlier versions: Arolsen 1992; Sydney 1995–96.
tracks.listen: How a dog of flowers came to Bilbao from Germany by way of Sydney, why "popular demand" is a myth, the twin in Connecticut, and how his coat is changed.

tracks.room: Museum plaza · the Txema Agirre plaque
tracks.title: Museum plaza — Txema Agirre
tracks.where: Beside the plaque in the small square just in front of Puppy, on the city side, where a plaque and a monolith remember Txema Agirre; stand to one side so others can read it [O2, ALT-P].
tracks.what: Memorial to José María Aguirre Larraona, "Txema Agirre", officer of the Ertzaintza (Basque police), shot on Monday 13 October 1997 beside the museum while checking a van; a plaque (installed after fourteen years) and a monolith in the small square in front of Puppy, which bears his name.
tracks.listen: Who Txema Agirre was, what happened here five days before the opening, and how he is remembered.

tracks.room: Museum plaza · facing the building, Calle Iparragirre behind you
tracks.title: Museum plaza — "Our town is dying"
tracks.where: On the Museum plaza, facing the whole front of the museum, with Calle Iparragirre, the long straight street into the city, at your back [O1]. The third paragraph (the competition) is cuttable for Highlights if O20 runs long.
tracks.what: The 1991 agreement between the Basque institutions and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation (Thomas Krens); the 1991 invited competition (Arata Isozaki, Coop Himmelb(l)au, Frank O. Gehry); the plaza and entrance on the Calle Iparragirre axis; the former wharf on the Nervión.
tracks.listen: How a city that said it was dying struck a hard bargain with New York, how Gehry won the job, and how his building meets the city's straight lines.

tracks.room: The broad stairway down to the Hall (heard walking)
tracks.title: The stairway — Going down to go in
tracks.where: Start it at the top of the broad stairway that leads down from the plaza to the entrance, and listen as you walk down into the Hall; nothing in it needs a view [O3, O4].
tracks.what: The descending entrance stairway (OUTSIDE); construction October 1993 – October 1997; executive architects IDOM (Bilbao); director Juan Ignacio Vidarte; main contractor Ferrovial; construction budget about US$100 million, delivered on time and on budget.
tracks.listen: Why you go down to go in, and how a building with no easy shapes was built in four years for the money agreed.

tracks.title: ZERO — The room that multiplies
tracks.where: In the Hall, just outside the door of ZERO, the small introductory room in the lobby; play it before you go in, standing clear of the doorway [O4].
tracks.what: ZERO, the museum's introductory gallery and immersive optical device in the lobby, a commission of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao created by Local Projects; curved projection with mirrors, a 300-degree view multiplying the room fourteen times; original soundtrack using the txalaparta; opened December 2018.
tracks.listen: How an underused lounge became a kaleidoscope, what it shows you about Bilbao and the building, and what to listen for.

tracks.title: Atrium — The heart of the building
tracks.where: Near the middle of the Atrium, the tall, light-filled space beyond the Hall, at a spot where you can look straight up to the skylight and, ideally, see the columns of red and blue words in gallery 101 [O5, O10].
tracks.what: The Atrium (55 m high, about 900 m²), with glass curtain walls, curved walkways, titanium-and-glass lifts and the metal-flower skylight; about twenty galleries, orthogonal and organic; Jenny Holzer's Installation for Bilbao, 1997/2017, gallery 101, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa (named in one version-neutral sentence).
tracks.listen: How tall the Atrium really is, how the whole building hangs on it, and what to look for when you look up.

tracks.title: Atrium — Holzer's columns of light
tracks.where: In the Atrium, at a spot where you can see into gallery 101 and its row of tall columns of moving red and blue words [O5].
tracks.what: Jenny Holzer, Installation for Bilbao, 1997/2017, electronic LED sign, site-specific dimensions, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, gallery 101: nine vertical, double-sided LED signboards, each more than 12 m tall; texts in Basque, Spanish and English from Arno. Also named: LIKE BEAUTY IN FLAMES (2021), augmented reality, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: Why these columns are not Holzer's famous one-liners, where their words come from, and how to read them.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 — The gallery under the bridge
tracks.where: Just inside the entrance of gallery 104, the long gallery that opens off the Atrium and runs under the bridge, where you can see down the length of the room past the great curved walls of weathering steel [O6].
tracks.what: Richard Serra (San Francisco 1938 – Long Island 2024), The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, weathering steel, eight sculptures, dimensions variable, about 1,034 tonnes in all, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, gallery 104 (about 130 × 30 m, column-free, under La Salve Bridge).
tracks.listen: The room built under a bridge, the eight steel sculptures that fill it, and how Serra meant you to walk them.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 — Walls that lean
tracks.where: Inside or beside the first sculptures at the Atrium end of gallery 104, the twisted steel walls nearest the entrance; ideally in the corridor between the two torqued ellipses [O6, ALT-S].
tracks.what: Richard Serra, The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa: the pieces nearest the Atrium end in David Zwirner's "foreground to rear" order, Torqued Spiral (Closed Open Closed Open Closed), 2003; Torqued Ellipse, 2003–04; Double Torqued Ellipse, 2003–04 (order and labels to confirm at O6).
tracks.listen: What "torqued" means, how Serra wanted these walls to be understood, and how to walk them.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 — Snake waited eight years
tracks.where: Inside gallery 104, beside or at one end of Snake, the piece among the eight whose label reads "Snake"; stand where you can walk its length without blocking its openings. [O6, ALT-S]
tracks.what: Richard Serra (San Francisco 1938 – Long Island 2024), Snake, 1994–97, weathering steel, part of The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, eight sculptures, dimensions variable, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: Why the oldest of Serra's eight pieces was the only part of The Matter of Time in this gallery for eight years, what shared the room with it at the opening, and what came after it.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 — Lost on purpose
tracks.where: Inside gallery 104, beside the two Torqued Spirals, the pieces whose labels read "Torqued Spiral (Right Left)" and "Torqued Spiral (Open Left Closed Right)"; play it at an opening, then walk in. [O6, ALT-S]
tracks.what: Richard Serra (San Francisco 1938 – Long Island 2024), Torqued Spiral (Right Left), 2003–04, and Torqued Spiral (Open Left Closed Right), 2003–04, weathering steel, part of The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, eight sculptures, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: What happens to your sense of direction, and of time, inside Serra's two spirals.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 — Torus and sphere
tracks.where: Inside gallery 104, by the last two pieces of the sequence, whose labels read "Between the Torus and the Sphere" and "Blind Spot Reversed"; stand where you can also see along the whole gallery. [O6, ALT-S]
tracks.what: Richard Serra (San Francisco 1938 – Long Island 2024), Between the Torus and the Sphere, 2003–05, and Blind Spot Reversed, 2003–05, weathering steel, part of The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, eight sculptures, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: The two pieces Serra cut from rings and spheres, the shipyard boy who became the sculptor, and the whole gallery in one look.

tracks.title: Gallery 104 · Extra · The Serra that vanished
tracks.where: Anywhere in gallery 104, for example on the walk back to the Atrium; it needs no view. [O6]
tracks.what: Richard Serra, Equal-Parallel: Guernica-Bengasi (Igual-paralelo: Guernica-Bengasi), made for the Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid, 1986, lost; replica 2009. Also Snake, 1994–97, The Matter of Time, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa.
tracks.listen: The Serra that really did go missing, and why it wasn't the one in this gallery.

tracks.title: Atrium terrace — Chillida and the river
tracks.where: On the terrace off the Atrium, on the river side, near the two dark steel sculptures by Eduardo Chillida, with the pond below the terrace in view. [O7, O17]
tracks.what: Eduardo Chillida (San Sebastián 1924 – San Sebastián 2002), Advice to Space V (Consejo al espacio V), 1993, steel, 305 × 143 × 207 cm, and Embrace XI (Besarkada XI), 1996, forged steel, 260 × 88 × 108 cm, both Atrium Terrace, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa. In view: the pond, with Anish Kapoor's Tall Tree & the Eye and Yves Klein's Fire Fountain; Maman only if visible.
tracks.listen: The two Basque steels that took Tulips' place on the terrace, the pond that honours the river, and the story of how this riverbank was chosen.

tracks.title: Second floor — Serra from above
tracks.where: On the second floor, at the balcony opposite gallery 204, looking down into gallery 104 and the eight steel sculptures of The Matter of Time. [O8, O9]
tracks.what: Richard Serra (San Francisco 1938 – Long Island 2024), The Matter of Time, 1994–2005, weathering steel, eight sculptures, dimensions variable, Gallery 104, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, seen from above.
tracks.listen: The Serra gallery from above: what the balcony reveals, and what it still hides.

tracks.title: Lifts and walkways — Every piece different
tracks.where: Start it in a glass lift as the doors close, or as you set off along the curved walkways and stairs toward the third floor; the second half plays as you step out among the curves and glass. Keep moving with the flow. [O8]
tracks.what: The building: Frank Gehry's design (1991–97), developed with CATIA; structural engineers SOM; executive architects IDOM; built by Ferrovial, October 1993 – October 1997; titanium cladding by Permasteelisa. No artwork.
tracks.listen: How a building with no two joints alike was drawn, engineered and put up, and the paper-crumpling joke it never deserved.

tracks.title: Third floor — The metal flower
tracks.where: On the third floor, at the balcony opposite gallery 304, looking out over the Atrium, with the flower-shaped skylight above and the walkways and glass lifts below. [O10]
tracks.what: The building: the Atrium and its skylight "in the shape of a metal flower", Frank Gehry (Toronto 1929 – Santa Monica 2025), Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, 1991–97. No artwork.
tracks.listen: The flower over the Atrium, the fish behind Gehry's curves, and his boast about straight lines.

tracks.room: Going down to the Hall (heard moving)
tracks.title: Going down — The Bilbao effect
tracks.where: Start it as you set off down from the third floor by a glass lift or the stairs; it needs no view until near the end, when you're among the people in the Atrium or the Hall. [O8, O11]
tracks.what: The museum and the "Bilbao effect": visitor figures, the museum's own impact studies, its critics, Frank Gehry's verdict and Juan Ignacio Vidarte's. No artwork.
tracks.listen: The numbers behind the "Bilbao effect", as the museum counts them, and the people who doubted it, including its architect.

tracks.title: The Hall · Extra · Opening day, 1997
tracks.where: In the Hall, the entrance hall at the foot of the broad stairway, somewhere out of the flow of people coming in. [O11]
tracks.what: The royal inauguration of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, Saturday 18 October 1997, and the public opening on 19 October 1997. No artwork.
tracks.listen: The day a king flipped a switch, who was there, who marched against it, and what one great architect is reported to have said.

tracks.room: Outside · on the way to the river walk (heard walking)
tracks.title: Outside — From shipyards to river walk
tracks.where: Start it as you leave the museum and keep it playing while you make your way round and down to the river walk, the promenade along the water on the river side of the building. It ends as you reach the pond beside the building, where a tall tree of silver balls stands in the water. [O11, O12, O13]
tracks.what: The museum's site and the riverbank of Abandoibarra: a former wharf "with port and industrial use on a curve of the Nervión" (museum); before, the Euskalduna shipyard (founded 1900, closed 1988), container storage, rail lines and docks; after, Bilbao Ría 2000 (1992) and the riverside avenue, "an open-air leisure area".
tracks.listen: How a working riverbank of shipyards, docks and rail lines became the promenade you are walking on, and where the museum fits in that change.

tracks.title: The pond — Tall Tree & the Eye
tracks.where: On the river walk by the pond on the river side of the building, wherever the tall tree of silver balls standing in the water is in clear view. [O13]
tracks.what: Anish Kapoor (Bombay, India, 1954), Tall Tree & the Eye, 2009, stainless steel and carbon steel, 1297 × 442 × 440 cm, 73 reflective spheres around three axes, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, "Currently on view (Pond)". Also: the pond itself, "a tribute to the Nervión estuary" (architecture route).
tracks.listen: How seventy-three mirrored balls put the river, the bridge, the museum and you into one shifting picture, and why Kapoor thinks that matters.

tracks.title: The pond — Frank O. Gehry's fog
tracks.where: Stay on the river walk by the pond, with the tall tree of silver balls in view; if the fog is running, stand where you can watch it spread over the water. [O13, O14, O19]
tracks.what: Fujiko Nakaya (Sapporo, Japan, 1933), Fog Sculpture #08025 (F.O.G.), 1998, water fog generated by 1,000 fog nozzles and a high-pressure pump/motor system, site-specific, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa; in the pool beside the riverfront facade; runs on the hour for about eight minutes.
tracks.listen: The dedication hidden in the title, the pavilion she wrapped in fog at the 1970 world's fair in Osaka, her snow-scientist father, and how to catch the fog.

tracks.title: The pond · Extra · Fire on the water
tracks.where: Anywhere on the river walk by the pond, with the tall tree of silver balls in view; the fire fountains are in this same pond. [O13, O19]
tracks.what: Yves Klein (Nice, France, 1928), Fire Fountain, dated 1961, medium "Fire", site-specific, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, "Currently on view (Pond)": "a row of five fire fountains" in a pool outside the building, lit only in the evening, for about an hour, in short bursts (WP-FIRE; AUDIT_V5_FACTS S9). Also: Chillida's Advice to Space V on the terrace, "a void of fire and heat" (callback; Full only).
tracks.listen: How a fountain of fire that Yves Klein described in a lecture in 1959 came to stand in this pond, and how to see it lit.

tracks.title: River walk — Maman
tracks.where: On the river walk by the footbridge, wherever the whole of the giant bronze spider is in view, legs and body together; stay on the path around her. [O14]
tracks.what: Louise Bourgeois (Paris, 1911 / New York, 2010), Maman, 1999, cast 2001, Edition 2/6 + A.P., bronze, marble and stainless steel, 927 × 891 × 1023 cm ("Almost 9 meters tall"), Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, "Currently on view (Exterior next to the footbridge)". Conceived as the inaugural commission for Tate Modern's Turbine Hall, May 2000; another cast in Ottawa (National Gallery of Canada).
tracks.listen: Why the most frightening creature on the river walk is a love letter to a mother, and why the museum reads her as protector and predator at once.

tracks.title: River walk — Titanium, stone and glass
tracks.where: On the river walk at a spot where the building's titanium skin comes close to the path, ideally with limestone and glass in the same view; look, don't touch. [O15]
tracks.what: The building's three materials: about 33,000 extremely thin titanium sheets (museum), about a third of a millimetre thick (0.38 mm, Ferrovial); limestone and glass. Gehry Partners, design; IDOM, executive architects; Frank Gehry (1929–2025).
tracks.listen: How a test sample pinned outside an office, a slump in the arms trade and a change to the backing made this skin, and why the Soviet-submarine story stays a legend.

tracks.room: River walk · La Salve Bridge, the tower in view
tracks.title: La Salve Bridge — The bridge, the tower and the red arches
tracks.where: On the river walk near La Salve Bridge, the big road bridge that crosses the end of the museum, at a spot where the bridge, the tall tower beside it and the red frame on the bridge are all in view. [O16]
tracks.what: La Salve Bridge, officially Príncipes de España, engineer Juan Batanero, built from 1968, opened 1972; Gehry's tower at the end of the building; Daniel Buren (Boulogne-Billancourt, France, 1938), Arcos rojos / Arku gorriak, 2007, for the museum's tenth anniversary, compact laminate sheets, aluminium, galvanised steel, PVC film, clear Plexiglas, LEDs and metal-halide projectors, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa, "Currently on view (La Salve Bridge)".
tracks.listen: How Gehry turned a big road bridge from an obstacle into part of his building, and how Buren's red arches made it "less brutal, but more visible".

tracks.room: River walk (anywhere; ideally with a view across the water)
tracks.title: River walk · Extra · The ones who lost
tracks.where: Anywhere on the river walk; it needs no particular view and points to nothing across the water. [O17]
tracks.what: The 1991 invited competition: Arata Isozaki, Coop Himmelb(l)au and Frank O. Gehry; Thomas Krens on the final choice; the Isozaki Towers named on the museum's architecture route; the route's list of "internationally renowned architects" in Bilbao.
tracks.listen: What became of the two architects who lost the competition for this museum, and how one of them ended up in Bilbao anyway.

tracks.room: River walk · by La Salve Bridge
tracks.title: River walk — "We all need love"
tracks.where: A quiet place on the river walk near La Salve Bridge, out of the way of passers-by, with the museum beside you. [O16]
tracks.what: Close of the tour. Frank Gehry (Toronto, 1929 – Santa Monica, 2025) on Bilbao, NPR 2015; the museum's visitors against the feasibility study; the collection's credit line, Guggenheim Bilbao Museoa; the fog, the fire and the walk round the building.
tracks.listen: The man who called the "Bilbao effect" nonsense explains what Bilbao gave him, and the whole visit is gathered up by the river.
